assumptions: source assumption: Qh, Qc and W are positive magnitudes with directions on schematics; heat pump mission is Qh into the warm space with Qh=Qc+W (OpenStax 15.5).
Same single operating point and test condition for Qh and W (single test or single-condition interpolation per agency COP definition); identical energy units for numerator and denominator.
No seasonal averaging, duct, defrost, or auxiliary accounting in this record; seasonal performance is the separate HSPF record.

gaps: Requires extensions: point heating heat delivery in J, point work input in J, dimensionless point COP meaning. Must not be coerced to seasonal delivered_heat/seasonal_performance or to electricity_cost inputs.
Candidate aliases: heating COP at a stated operating condition; refrigerator COP (Qc/W) is a different record, not an inverse view.

models.inverse_notes: Qh and positive COP give W=Qh/COP; W and COP give Qh=COP*W. Zero-Qh with positive W gives COP 0 (degenerate no-delivery boundary, not a useful heat pump). Zero W is excluded (no drive). Substitution checked: Qh=5.30, W=1.0 gives COP 5.30; inversion W=5.30/5.30=1.0. Algebraic inversion does not establish that a field unit achieves the Carnot bound.
limitations: Excludes seasonal averaging (HSPF/HSPF2), EER in Btu/Wh, and refrigerator COPref=Qc/W; COPref=COP_hp-1 is a separate relation not curated here.
Real units range about 2-4 and degrade in very cold climates; Carnot value is an ideal upper bound between stated reservoir temperatures, not a default efficiency.

references.method: Published result: OpenStax Eqs. 15.40-15.42 compute Carnot COP 1/0.1887=5.30 and state Qh=5.30W between Th=318K and Tc=258K. Replay 5.3/1.0=5.3 exact; tolerance 0.01 covers the reported two-decimal rounding (half unit 0.005).
references.provenance: Published textbook ideal (Carnot) worked example, not a field measurement

references.method: Published consumer illustration: UMD Extension states COP=3.0 means about three units of heat per unit of electricity, inside OpenStax real range 2-4. Replay 3.0/1.0=3.0 exact.
references.provenance: Published Extension fact-sheet example consistent with textbook real range; independent operating-point illustration

rejection_cases.reason: Zero work input cannot drive cold-to-hot transfer; guard W>0 rejects division by zero and the free-heating implication.
Work input W is required; delivered heat alone does not determine COP.

relationship.locator: Sec. 15.5 Heat Pumps, Eq. 15.37 (COPhp=Qh/W) with Eqs. 15.38-15.42 Carnot evaluation and real-range prose; ENERGY STAR COP note (single-test rate ratio, dimensionless) corroborates operating-point scope
relationship.original_equation: COPhp = Qh/W (Eq. 15.37); COPhp = 1/Eff = 5.30 and Qh = 5.30W (Eqs. 15.40-15.42) for Th=45.0C, Tc=-15.0C
relationship.translation_notes: Direct transcription: source Qh (heat to warm space), W (work input) mapped to locals. Units normalized to J/J so COP is dimensionless (1); any identical energy units cancel. Dimensional check: energy/energy = dimensionless. Point scope retained: single operating condition, not seasonal; no temperature inputs in this record.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: quality of a heat pump is judged by Qh into the warm space vs work W; COP_hp=Qh/W (15.37); since Eff=W/Qh, COP=1/Eff>1; Carnot example Th=318K/Tc=258K gives Eff 0.1887, COP 5.30, Qh=5.30W; real heat pumps range about 2-4 so Qh is 2-4x W.

assumptions: source assumption: Region IV seasonal accounting per 10 CFR 430 App. M/M1; numerator is total seasonal space heating required and denominator is total seasonal electrical energy in the same season (ENERGY STAR note 4).
Same heat-pump system, same heating season, and same test procedure (Appendix M for HSPF, M1 for HSPF2) for Q, W, and HSPF; HSPF vs HSPF2 differ by procedure version, not by equation form.
Units as rated: Q in Btu, W in Wh, HSPF in Btu/Wh; conversion to dimensionless SPF needs division by 3.412 Wh/Btu-class factor handled outside this record.

gaps: Requires extensions: seasonal heating energy in Btu, seasonal electrical energy in Wh, seasonal performance in Btu/Wh. No current runtime unit or meaning fits; do not coerce to dimensionless seasonal_performance or kWh electricity_consumption.
HSPF2 vs HSPF is a procedure-version label (M1 vs M), not a separate equation; dimensionless SPF = HSPF/3.412-class conversion needs a separate adapter, not silently substituted.

models.inverse_notes: Q with positive HSPF gives W=Q/HSPF; Q and W with positive W give HSPF=Q/W. Zero seasonal electricity with zero seasonal heat leaves HSPF underdetermined (0/0); zero W with positive Q is excluded as a domain violation of the same-season accounting. Substitution checked: Q=7800, W=1000 gives HSPF=7.8. Seasonal inversion does not recover operating-point COP.
limitations: Rating-procedure scope only (Region IV, App. M/M1); field performance adds ducts, defrost, sizing, auxiliaries, and climate differences not in this record.
Excludes dimensionless SPF, SEER/SEER2, and EER/EER2; HSPF values such as 7.8/8.1/8.5/11 are threshold examples, not defaults for any house or climate.

references.method: Independent arithmetic illustration of the agency-defined quotient: ENERGY STAR defines HSPF2 as seasonal Btu over seasonal Wh, so 7.8 Btu/Wh * 1000 Wh = 7800 Btu. No published seasonal Q/W pair was found; 7.8 is the ENERGY STAR split-system threshold used only as an illustrative input, not a default. Replay exact.
references.provenance: Independent elementary illustration of the rated definition; not a field measurement

references.method: Independent illustration at a materially different scale: cold-climate non-ducted threshold 8.5 Btu/Wh with 2000 Wh gives 17000 Btu under the same definition. Replay exact.
references.provenance: Independent elementary illustration of the rated definition; not a field measurement

assumptions: source assumption: single homogeneous plane layer under steady 1D conduction with uniform thickness, constant conductivity, equal face areas, and negligible lateral escape (Univ. Physics 1.6 slab/rod setup).
Same layer, material, thickness interval, area, and conductivity reference for L, k, A, and Rth; faces isothermal.
Area-normalized R=L/k (b01) and absolute Rth=R/A are linked by the stated equal-area scope; unequal areas need 3D treatment outside this record.

gaps: Requires extensions: conduction_thickness (m), thermal_conductivity (W/(m*K)), heat_transfer_area (m2), absolute thermal resistance (K/W). Distinct from b01 area-normalized R (m2*K/W); the bridge is Rth=R/A for equal areas.
Candidate alias: conduction thermal resistance in K/W for one layer; convective 1/(hA) and series sums need separate records.

models.inverse_notes: Rth with known k,A gives L=Rth*k*A; with known L,A gives k=L/(Rth*A); with known L,k gives A=L/(Rth*k); all require the other two strictly positive. Zero thickness/area/conductivity excluded (no layer or infinite resistance). Substitution checked: Rth=39.8089, k=80, A=7.85e-05 gives L=39.8089*80*7.85e-05=0.25 m.
limitations: One-layer absolute resistance only; composite series/parallel sums and film coefficients are excluded though the source discusses the circuit analogy.
Excludes temperature/moisture-dependent k, contact resistance, and IP R units; table k values are near-0C representatives, not defaults.

references.method: Published inputs with arithmetic replay: Univ. Physics rods L=0.25 m, k=80 W/m*C, A=7.85e-05 m2 give 0.25/(80*7.85e-05)=39.8089 K/W; expected 39.81 K/W. Tolerance 0.05 covers the 3-significant rounding of A and the reported joint-T/rate rounding. Alternate-route check reported steel dT=58.7K over P=1.47W gives 39.93 K/W, consistent within that rounding.
references.provenance: Source-backed derivation from published geometry/conductivity with reported-dT-over-P consistency check

references.method: Published inputs at materially different conductivity: L=0.25, k=220, A=7.85e-05 give 14.4760 K/W; expected 14.48 K/W. Tolerance 0.05 covers rounding. Alternate route reported Al dT=21.3K/1.47W=14.49 K/W, consistent.
references.provenance: Source-backed derivation with reported-dT-over-P consistency check (aluminum branch)

rejection_cases.reason: Zero area ceases to describe a 1D slab path (infinite resistance limit); guard A>0 rejects it.
Conductivity k is required; geometry alone does not determine resistance.

relationship.locator: Univ. Physics Sec. 1.6: Eq. 1.9 (P=kA(Th-Tc)/d), two-conductor second Solution ('Recall R=L/k; P=ADeltaT/R'), and Significance note ('resistance corresponds to R/A'); b01 plane-layer R record dependency
relationship.original_equation: R = L/k; P = ADeltaT/R; absolute resistance = R/A = L/(kA)
relationship.translation_notes: Derived definition (dependency identified): from source P=A*dT/R with R=L/k, define absolute Rth=dT/P=R/A=L/(kA). Local L renames source d/L thickness. Units: m/((W/(m*K))*m2)=K/W. Dimensional check: length/(conductivity*area)=temperature/power. Equal-area 1D scope retained; C-degree/W identical to K/W for differences.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: slab rate P=kA(Th-Tc)/d (Eq. 1.9); second solution recalls R=L/k with P=ADeltaT/R and evaluates Rsteel=3.13e-3 and RAl=1.14e-3 m2*C/W for 0.25 m rods of area 7.85e-05 m2, adding R factors in series; Significance note states the resistance corresponds to R/A and is additive even for unequal areas.

assumptions: source assumption: homogeneous substance (solids/liquids grouping in Table 11.1) with tabulated density for the substance and phase; volume occupied by that mass.
Same substance sample, phase, and condition for rho, V, and m; gas compressibility/condition dependence excluded from this condensed-matter profile.
SI coherence: rho in kg/m3 with V in m3 gives m in kg; the source notes 1 g/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3 and water 1000 kg/m3 basis.

gaps: Requires extensions: density in kg/m3 and volume in m3; mass in kg reuses b01 mass quantity. No runtime unit fits rho or V.
Supports b01 sensible-heat mass sourcing (e.g., water volume to mass via 1000 kg/m3); not a thermal law itself, included to explain source scope per assignment boundaries.

models.inverse_notes: m with positive rho gives V=m/rho; m with nonnegative V gives rho=m/V requiring V>0. Zero volume with zero mass leaves density underdetermined (0/0). Substitution checked: m=2.00e12, rho=1000 gives V=2.00e9 m3. Inversion does not identify composition (different substances can share a density).
limitations: Condensed-matter profile only as applied here; gases need stated T/p condition (Table 11.1 gas columns) and are excluded from reuse as defaults.
Excludes voids, mixtures, and buoyancy/floatation inferences; density identifies composition only with other evidence.

references.method: Published result: OpenStax Eqs. 11.4-11.5 compute V=Ah=50.0 km2*40.0 m=2.00e9 m3 and m=rho*V=1.00e3*2.00e9=2.00e12 kg. Replay exact in integer-exact double range; tolerance 1e6 kg is far below the 3-significant display rounding (half unit 5e9 kg) and above floating error.
references.provenance: Published textbook worked example (reservoir mass from volume) with water density from Table 11.1

references.method: Published supporting step: OpenStax 14.2 solution states 0.250 L water has mass 0.250 kg via density 1000 kg/m3 (1 L = 1 kg); V=2.50e-4 m3 times 1000 gives 0.25 kg exact. Materially different scale from the reservoir case.
references.provenance: Published textbook supporting computation (water-volume to mass) converted from L to m3

rejection_cases.reason: Zero density ceases to describe condensed matter; guard rho>0 rejects it (vacuum needs a different model).
Density rho is required; volume alone does not determine mass.

relationship.locator: Sec. 11.2, Eqs. 11.1-11.3 (rho=m/V) solved as m=rhoV with Eqs. 11.4-11.5 reservoir evaluation and Table 11.1 densities
relationship.original_equation: rho = m/V (Eqs. 11.1-11.2); solved m = rhoV; reservoir V=Ah=2.00e9 m3, m=1.00e3*2.00e9=2.00e12 kg (Eqs. 11.4-11.5)
relationship.translation_notes: Algebraic rearrangement of the defined quotient rho=m/V into computable m=rho*V; no unit normalization beyond SI (kg/m3 * m3 = kg). Dimensional check: (mass/length^3)*length^3=mass. Condensed-matter application profile stated separately; gas T/p dependence noted in limitations.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: density is mass per unit volume rho=m/V (Eqs. 11.1-11.2) in kg/m3 with Table 11.1 values (water 1.000e3, aluminum 2.7e3, etc.); reservoir example solves for m=rhoV with V=Ah=2.00e9 m3 and water 1.00e3 to get m=2.00e12 kg (Eqs. 11.3-11.5).
